imports.text: imports bring in the tools: JSON, the environment, the system, paths, the Bedrock client, its config, and .env loading.

setup.text: load_dotenv reads the credentials from the .env file next to the script.

prompt.text: PROMPT instructs the model to split a numbered source file into sections and blocks, write one plain-English sentence per block, and return a single JSON object mapping each block to its line ranges.

functions.text: ask creates a Bedrock client, sends the prompt to the configured model, asserts the reply is complete, and returns the JSON object extracted from the raw text.
check verifies the map: no duplicate text id, every text has content and line ranges, every range is in bounds, no line belongs to two blocks, and every non-blank line belongs to at least one block.
write_map writes the map to a file as a formatted JSON object, with the file key first and each section key holding a pretty-printed array of text objects.

main.text: main's first stage reads the source file from the command-line argument and splits it into lines.
main's second stage builds the numbered code string and formats it into the base prompt.
main's third stage asks the model up to three times, checks each answer, and on a broken rule sends the answer and the error back for repair.
main's fourth stage writes the valid map to map.json next to the source file and prints the block count.

entry.text: entry point calls main when the script runs directly.
